question: An engineer needs to perform a backup of user roles and locales from Cisco UCS Manager to replicate the setting to a different fabric interconnect. The engineer wants to review the file before importing it to a target fabric interconnect. Which backup type must be selected to meet these requirements?
theory: A System Configuration backup is an XML export limited to system-level settings such as usernames, roles, and locales — exactly what's needed to replicate access-control configuration to a different fabric interconnect. Because it is XML (human-readable and reviewable before import), unlike the binary Full State backup, and because it excludes service profiles/VLANs/VSANs (which belong to Logical Configuration) and doesn't bundle everything together (as All Configuration does), System Configuration is the precise, minimal backup type for this AAA/RBAC-focused requirement. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 14 — UCS Configuration Management, System Configuration Backup)
